question.text: An SIA is scoping an impact assessment engagement and needs to confirm that the donor company is itself CSR-liable under Section 135 of the Companies Act 2013. Which of the following threshold sets triggers CSR applicability (any ONE being sufficient)?

answer.text: Net worth >= INR 100 cr OR turnover >= INR 500 cr OR net profit >= INR 2 cr
Net worth >= INR 500 cr OR turnover >= INR 1,000 cr OR net profit >= INR 5 cr
Net worth >= INR 1,000 cr AND turnover >= INR 500 cr AND net profit >= INR 10 cr
Only listed companies with market capitalisation above INR 500 cr are CSR-liable

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 135(1) of the Companies Act 2013 makes CSR obligations applicable to every company (including a foreign company) that meets ANY ONE of three thresholds in the immediately preceding financial year: net worth >= INR 500 crore, OR turnover >= INR 1,000 crore, OR net profit >= INR 5 crore. The trigger is disjunctive, so meeting a single one of these is enough to bring the company within Section 135. The Trap: The INR 100 cr / INR 500 cr / INR 2 cr set is a pre-amendment / fabricated bundle. Using "AND" wrongly requires all three thresholds to be breached simultaneously. Market capitalisation is not part of the Section 135 test — applicability is not limited to listed companies above a particular market cap. Note: The Social Impact Assessors workbook references CSR applicability in general terms but does not, on the cited pages, list the specific INR 500 cr / INR 1,000 cr / INR 5 cr thresholds verbatim. Those thresholds are drawn from Section 135(1) of the Companies Act 2013 rather than from the workbook pages checked.
